documentation.content:
The alert Cloud Function logged a delivery failure.

**Why this policy exists.** Until 2026-11-15 a failed alert delivery was silent: `process_alert` swallowed every exception, Pub/Sub acked, and the alert was dropped with nothing but a log line nobody read. The 50-attempt dead-letter policy could not engage. Delivery failures now re-raise (total failure only) so Pub/Sub retries and eventually dead-letters -- but **the DLQ is forensic and nobody watches it**, so without this policy a retry exhaustion would still be silent. This policy is the part that tells a human.

**Note the filter matches `textPayload`, not severity.** Every application log line from this function lands at severity DEFAULT in `run.googleapis.com/stderr` with no `severity` field at all, so a `severity>=WARNING` condition would match nothing.

**Triage.** Check the DLQ for what was lost:
`gcloud pubsub subscriptions pull calypso-alerts-dlq-sub --project=calypso-trading-bot --limit=10 --auto-ack`
Then the function's own records:
`gcloud logging read 'resource.labels.service_name="process-trading-alert"' --project=calypso-trading-bot --freshness=1d`

conditionMatchedLog.filter: resource.type="cloud_run_revision" AND resource.labels.service_name="process-trading-alert" AND (textPayload:"ALERT DELIVERY FAILED" OR textPayload:"Failed to send email" OR textPayload:"Telegram send failed" OR textPayload:"Failed to send Telegram message" OR textPayload:"Telegram delivery exception" OR textPayload:"Email delivery exception" OR textPayload:"Error processing alert" OR textPayload:"no recipient configured" OR textPayload:"not configured")
